core_obligations: Set up the criterion for affineness through the limit presentation of X, as invoked at the start of the proof (proof lines 8967-8969).
Use the hypotheses that T is affine, X is quasi-separated, X has finitely many generic points, and that T^0 -> X^0 is injective with the local rings O_{X,x_j} = O_{T,t_j} (proof lines 8957-8963).
Build an affine open of X containing the images x_1, ..., x_m and conclude, completing the argument up to line 9014.
proof_roadmap: Invoke the affineness criterion attached to the limit presentation.
Exploit the generic-point bijection and the local ring identifications.
Produce the affine open containing the prescribed points.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for a finite set of points of X to lie in an affine open, formulated through an auxiliary affine T mapping to X: if the generic points of T map bijectively into the generic points of X and the local rings at the chosen points agree, then the points of X lie in an affine open. The proof uses the criterion for affineness via the limit presentation of X, and the reduction of the given data along the morphism T -> X to build the required affine open; the argument occupies lines 8967-9014 and involves the identification of the local rings and the generic-point hypothesis. H3: the interplay between the generic-point condition, the local ring identification and the affine criterion for the limit presentation is independent work.
